title: UN committee backs Rohingya resolution calling for aid funding
excerpt: The text, passed 128 to 6, asks for steady funding for the 2026 Joint Response Plan and full humanitarian access. Bangladesh says repatriation has stalled.

image.alt: Rows of seats in the United Nations General Assembly Hall in New York
image.credit: Basil D Soufi / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

content:
The UN General Assembly's Third Committee on Wednesday (18 November) adopted a resolution on the "Situation of human rights of Rohingya Muslims and other minorities in Myanmar", The Business Standard reported, citing BSS. The vote was 128 in favour, 6 against and 33 abstentions.

The resolution, led by the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the European Union, names grave violations by both the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army. It calls for unhindered humanitarian access, sustained funding for the Rohingya response, including the 2026 Joint Response Plan, and protection of Rohingya political rights, including voting rights.

What Bangladesh said

Shanchita Haque, Bangladesh's Chargé d'Affaires to the UN, told the committee there had been "no meaningful progress" on repatriation nine years after the mass displacement.

The United States asked for a recorded vote because the text mentions the International Criminal Court. It also praised Bangladesh for hosting more than 1.2 million Rohingya.

Why it matters

The vote came a day before the International Court of Justice was due to deliver its judgment in The Gambia v Myanmar. For agencies in Cox's Bazar, the most practical part of the text is its call for sustained funding and access, which gives them UN language to use in appeals for the response.

What to watch

UN General Assembly President Khalilur Rahman visits the Cox's Bazar camps on Friday (20 November) to hear from refugees, with a joint press conference with UN Resident Coordinator Carol Flore-Smereczniak, UNB reported. Watch whether donors follow the resolution with new pledges.
